<sense>

<senses>
<sense>
<definition> , v. 
<xref rid="A00626">אָוָה I</xref>) 
<italic>desire, appetite</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Midr. Till. to Ps. CXX עושה תַאֲוַת נפשו לשעה he satisfies the lust of his soul for the moment; עושה תַאֲוָתוֹ לשעה. Erub. 54
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to Ps. XXI, 3) זכה תאות לבו וכ' if he is worthy, thou grantest him the desire of his heart (without prayer), if he is not worthy, thou refusest him not the prayer of his lips. Sot. 47
<sup>a</sup> תאותו מיהא וכ' his desire at least was to curse. Pirké d’R. El. ch. XXXVII לא עלתה בידו תאותו he did not succeed in doing what he had desired to do. Tosef. Ber. V, 1; Y. Pes. X, beg. 37
<sup>b</sup> בת' with an appetite for food, v. תָּאֵב; [Bab. ib. 99
<sup>b</sup> כשהוא ת', v. תָּאַב]; Y. Succ. II, 53
<sup>a</sup> bot.; a. fr.—בשר ת', v. בָּשָׂר.—Esp. 
<italic>sexual desire</italic>. Y. Meg. IV, 75
<sup>a</sup> מכניס אהבה ומוציא ת' it (garlic) causes love to enter, and the sexual desire to come forth. Lev. R. s. 18; Koh. R. to XII, 5 (ref. to אביונה, ib.) זו הת' this means the sexual desire. Gen. R. s. 85 מלאך … הת' the angel that is appointed over marital life. Ab. IV, 21 הקנאה והת' וכ' envy, voluptuousness, and ambition take man away from this world (accelerate his death); a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="V00017">
<head-word>תְּאוֹם</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083"> תָּאַם)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>twin.</italic></definition>
<notes>
<italic>—Pl.</italic> תְּאוֹמִים. Cant. R. to V, 2 (play on תמתי, ib.) תְּאוֹמָתִי מה הת' הללו וכ' my twin sister, as in the case of twins, when one has a headache, the other feels it, so, as it were, does the Lord say, ‘with him (Israel) am I in distress’ (Ps. XCI, 15). Gen. R. s. 85; a. e.—Esp. 
<italic>Gemini</italic>, a constellation of the Zodiac. Pesik. R. s. 20 מזל ת' אדם (read: מזל אדם ת') man’s planet is Gemini. Tanḥ. Haăz. 1 [read:] וכשגדל נעשה כת' כלומר שלם וכ' when man grows up, he becomes like the planet Gemini, that is to say, perfect &c.—Fem. תְּאוֹמָה. Cant. R. l. c., v. supra. Ib. תאומתי כביכול, v. תְּיוֹמֶת. Gen. R. s. 22 קין ותְאוֹמָתוֹ Cain and his twin sister. Ib. ת' יתירה נולדה וכ' an additional twin sister was born with Abel; a. e.—
<plural-form>Pl. תְּאוֹמוֹת</plural-form>. Ib. הבל ושתי תְאוֹמוֹתָיו Abel and his two sisters born with him.—Trnsf. תְּאוֹמוֹת (from their shape) 
<italic>molar teeth</italic>. Bekh. VI, 4 (39
<sup>a</sup>) Ar. (Mish. ed. מַתְאִימוֹת; Bab. ed. תיומת).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="V00025">
<head-word>תָּאַם</head-word>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> v. 
<xref rid="A01960">אַם</xref>) 
<italic>to join, combine</italic>.</definition>
<notes>—Denom. תְּאוֹם.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְאִים</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (denom. of תְּאוֹם) 
<italic>to be twin-like, joined, adjoining</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Ber. III, 6
<sup>b</sup> top היו שם שתי דרכים מַתְאִימוֹת וכ' if there are two twin-roads (starting from, and leading to the same place), one long, but levitically clean, and the other short, but unclean; Y. Naz. VII, 56
<sup>a</sup> bot. Tosef. Sabb. III, 3 שתי כירים המתאימות two adjoining stoves (perfectly alike); Sabb. 37
<sup>a</sup>; Y. ib. III, beg. 5
<sup>c</sup>; a. e.—Bekh. VI, 1 מתאימות (sub. שינים) 
<italic>molar teeth</italic>, v. תְּאוֹם.—Kel. II, 7 Ar., v. infra.—Part. pass. מוּתְאָם; f. מוּתְאֶמֶת; 
<plural-form>pl. מוּתְאָמִים; מוּתְאָמוֹת</plural-form>
<italic>a</italic>) 
<italic>placed between</italic>. Cant. R. to I, 13 שהוא מ' בין וכ' he (Abraham) was between the Divine Presence and the angel. Ib. to IV, 2; Yalk. ib. 988 שהיו מ' וכ' they (the Israelites) were between &c. Cant. R. to IV, 4 שהיו מ' בין החלוץ וכ' they were placed between the vanguard and the rear-guard.—
<italic>b</italic>) 
<italic>divided into two compartments</italic>. Sifré Deut. 357 as the branch is separated from the trunk, yet not detached (v. פִּסְגָּה), כך קבורתו … מ' מן ההר ואינה מ' so is Moses’ grave divided off from the mountain and yet not entirely divided off, the valley being between them (to connect them); Yalk. ib. 963.—Kel. II, 7 קלמרים המותאמות ed. Dehr. (oth. ed. המְתוֹאָמוֹת, 
<italic>Pu.</italic>; Ar. המַתְאֶמֶת) an inkstand with two compartments, v. קַלְמָרִין.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>fig-tree; fig.</italic> Cant. R. to VI, 2 הת' הזו … יפה לה ויפה לת' when the fig-tree is plucked in due time, it is good for it and good for the fig; Gen. R. s. 62; Koh. R. to V, 11.</definition>
<notes> Ib.; Y. Ber. II, 5
<sup>c</sup> top בעל הת' יוֹדע וכ' the owner of the fig-tree knows when it is time to pluck it (God knows when it is time to call the righteous away). Gen. R. l. c. היו … תחת ת' אחת were wont to rise early and sit down under a certain fig-tree to study; ib. חדא … תְּאֵינָתִי וכ' the one benefit that you conferred upon me by sitting and studying under my fig-tree, you have now taken away; Yalk. ib. 110; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. תְּאֵנִים, תְּאַנוֹת, תְּאֵי'</plural-form>
<italic>figs</italic>. Y. Ber. l. c. תְּאֵינוֹתָיו, v. תָּלַע. B. Mets. VII, 4. Ber. 41
<sup>b</sup> הביאו לפניהם ת' וכ' if figs and grapes are placed before diners during the meal. Ib. VI, 8. Ib. 44
<sup>a</sup> קוצצי ת' fig-cutters; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> עֵין ת'
<pos> pr. n. pl.</pos>
<italic>ʿEn-T’enah</italic>, near Sepphoris.</definition>

<entry id="V00035">
<head-word>תֵּבָה</head-word>
<head-word>תֵּיבָה</head-word>
<language-key>(b. h. </language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="unknown">תֵּבָה; Egyptian; v.</xref>, however,
<xref rid="A00083"> תָּבָא)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>ship, ark, chest</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 31 (play on קנים, Gen. VI, 14) מה הקן … אף תֵּיבָתְךָ וכ' as birds (v. קֵן) make the leper clean, so does thy ark cleanse thee. Ib. על שם תֵּיבָתוֹ של נח (it is called 
<italic>t’biḳin</italic>) from the measures of Noah’s ark. Y. Erub. V, 22
<sup>c</sup> bot. כיצד היו ישראל … כת' how did the Israelites march in the desert?… like a chest (forming a square), opp. כקורה like a beam (in columns). Men. 94
<sup>b</sup> כמין ת' פרוצה (the shape of the show-bread was) that of an open chest (without a lid and with a level bottom), opp. כמין ספינה רוקדת like a rocking ship (with a curved bottom). Sifra M’tsorʿa, Zab., Par. 1, ch. II תֵּיבַת הבלנים the bathers’ chest. Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. X, 1, sq.; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. תֵּבוֹת, תֵּי'</plural-form>. Midr. Till. to Ps. I היה צריך לעשות ת' הרבה he would have been obliged to build many arks. Y. Sot. VIII, beg. 22
<sup>b</sup> שהיו עשויין ת' ת' they (the Egyptians) were arrayed in squares.—Esp. 
<italic>the chest in the synagogue containing the scrolls of the Pentateuch</italic>. Sot. 38
<sup>b</sup>, v. פְּסַק. Taan. II, 1 מוציאין את הת' וכ' (at prayer meetings) they bring the chest out to the open place of the town, and put ashes of wood on the chest &c. Meg. III, 1 בני העיר … בה"כ לוקחין ת' ת' וכ' if the citizens of a township sell … a synagogue, they may buy (for the money) a book chest; if they sell a chest, they may buy book wrappers; a. fr.—עבר לפני הת', ירד לפני הת' to go before the chest, 
<italic>to act as reader of prayers</italic>. Ber. 34
<sup>a</sup> שירד לפני הת' וכ' who recited the prayers in the presence of &c. Ib. V, 3 העובר לפני הת' וטעה וכ' if a reader makes a mistake (reads heretical formulas), another person must pass before the chest in his place. Ib. 4. Ib. 34
<sup>a</sup> העובר לפני הת' צריך לסרב he that is asked to read the prayers &c., v. סָרַב. Taan. II, 2 מורידין לפני הת' וכ' we depute as reader (on fast days) an old man &c.; a. v. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>word</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Men. 30
<sup>b</sup> ת' בת שתי וכ' a word of two letters. Sabb. 104
<sup>a</sup> they did not know הי באמצע ת' וכ' in which (of the two forms of the letters מנצפ"ך) were to be employed in the middle of a word, and which at the end; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. תֵּיבוֹת, תֵּיבִיּוֹת</plural-form>. Ḥull. 64
<sup>b</sup> דפסק … ת' (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 40) where the scribe divides them into two words; ib. 65
<sup>a</sup>. Y. Meg. I, 71
<sup>c</sup> bot. תיביות; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to ask, claim, summon</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Keth. V, 2 נותנין … משתְּבָעָהּ הבעל וכ' to a maiden we allow twelve months from the time that her intended husband claims her, to prepare her outfit. Nidd. 66
<sup>a</sup> תְּבָעוּהָ לינשא וכ' when they ask her to make ready for the wedding, and she is satisfied (to do so at once); Yeb. 37
<sup>b</sup>. Keth. 64
<sup>a</sup> תָּבְעָה היא if she demands her marital rights. Erub. 100
<sup>b</sup> האשה תוֹבַעַת … תּוֹבֵע וכ' the woman asks for gratification in her heart, and the man with his mouth. Shebu. 40
<sup>b</sup> חזקה אין אדם תובע אלא וכ' the legal presumption is that nobody will sue a neighbor, unless he has some claim against him. Pesik. Baḥod., p. 104
<sup>a</sup>, sq. אני תובע בה I shall propose marriage to her, v. אֲלִיקִי. Sifré Deut. 16 (ref. to Deut. I, 16) צדיק בצדקו תובע ומביא ראיות the righteous in his righteousness claims and offers evidence, i.e. the judge must not be guided by his moral conviction or by the reputation of the claimant, but by evidence only. Midr. Till. to Ps. VII כל התועב את עצמו וכ' (prob. to be read: התובע את עלבונו) he who asks (God) to resent the insult offered to him will not be punished for it; a. fr.—[Tanḥ. ed. Bub. Balak 18 תובען; Yalk. Num. 766 תובעין, v. טָבַע II.]—Part. pass. תָּבוּעַ; f. תְּבוּעָה. Keth. 57
<sup>b</sup> בגרה הרי היא כת' if she is of age, she is considered as having been asked to prepare for the wedding; כת' דבתולה as the maiden that has been asked (to whom twelve months are allowed); כת' דאלמנה as the widow that has been asked (to whom one month only is allowed).</notes></sense></senses>

<sense>

<sup>b</sup>; Yalk. Ex. 164 תבען … ולא נִתְבָּעוֹת he proposed to them a sinful act, and they refused. Ib. 286 נִתְבְּעוּ … בתורה וכ' the nations of the world were asked to receive the Law, in order not to give them an excuse for saying, אילו נִתְבַּעְנוּ וכ' had we been asked, we might have accepted it &c.; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<italic>deep, depth, interior of the earth</italic>. Gen. R. s. 2 (ref. to Gen. I, 2) זו מלכות … כמו הת' ‘the deep’, that is the wicked (Roman) empire which is unfathomable as the deep; מה הת' הזה וכ' as the deep cannot be searched out, so the wicked &c. Y. Ḥag. II, 77

A corpse buried in stubble, straw, earth, or pebbles, but if buried in water &c., it does not make a grave of the depth (does not make unclean that which was above it before discovery). Ib. אי זהו קבר הת' … זוכרו a grave of the depth is one that nobody remembers to have existed; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. תְּהוֹמוֹת</plural-form>. Mekh. B’shall., Shir., s. 5, v. עִשּׁוֹנִית; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="V00122">
<head-word>תהי</head-word>
<head-word>תָּהָא</head-word>

<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (cmp. שָׁהָא) [
<italic>to stand still</italic>,] </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to gaze, be astonished; to be confounded, be waste</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 2, beg., v. בָּהָא. Ib., end כבר … יושב ותוֹהֵא once R. S. b. Z. sat gazing (deep in thought, absent-minded). Taan. 6
<sup>b</sup> (play on ת̇מ̇ט̇ר̇, Am. IV, 7) ת̇הא מקום מ̇ט̇ר̇ the place where the rain fell became waste (through destructive showers); a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to pause, bethink one’s self</italic>
<italic>, regret</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Taan. III, 66
<sup>c</sup> bot. שלשה … ות' שבראן three things God created, and regretted that he had created them. Ib. I, 65
<sup>b</sup> bot. (ref. to Num. XXIII, 19) אם יאמר לך אדם … בן אדם אני סופו לִתְהוֹת בו וכ' if a man says to thee, I am a God, he lies; (if he says,) I am the son of man, he shall regret it; (and if he says,) I will rise to heaven, he says, but he shall not fulfill it. Y. Ned. I, 36
<sup>d</sup> bot. [read:] מכיון שנודר … סופו לתהות מכיון שהוא תוהא וכ' when one vows in rashness, he will finally regret it, and when he does regret, his sacrifices are like slaughtering profane beasts in the Temple court. Kidd. 40
<sup>b</sup> בתוהא על הראשונות when he is sorry for his good deeds in the past; Y. Peah I, 16
<sup>b</sup> top. Num. R. s. 10, beg. בתוהא על הראשונות (not הרשע; ed. Wil. בתוֹהֶה) when he (the wicked) regrets his doings in the past. Ex. R. s. 20
<sup>2</sup> התחיל המוכר תוהא the seller was sorry; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="V00202">
<head-word>תּוֹכֵחָה</head-word>
<head-word>תּוֹכַחַת</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083"> יָכַח)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>reproof, admonition, threat of punishment</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Arakh. 16
<sup>b</sup> תמיהני … שמקבל ת' I wonder whether in this generation there is one that accepts admonition; Sifra K’dosch., Par. 2, ch. IV. Arakh. l. c. עד היכן ת' וכ' how far must you go in reproving your neighbor (Lev. XIX, 17)? Until he strikes you. Lev. R. s. 27 (ref. to Is. I, 18) זו תשובה וזו ת' is this an argument, and this a threat?; Tanḥ. Emor 10; Yalk. Mic. 554. Ḥag. 4
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to Gen. XLV, 3) ומה ת' של בשר ודם כך ת' וכ' if the rebuke of a human being has such an effect, how much greater ought to be the effect of God’s rebuke!; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. תּוֹכָחוֹת</plural-form>. Tam. 28
<sup>a</sup> יאהב את הת' שכל זמן שת' וכ' let man love reproofs, for as long as reproofs are in the world, ease of mind comes upon the world, good, and blessing &c. Deut. R. s. 1 ראויין היו הת' וכ' the rebukes (threats of punishment) should have been pronounced through Balaam, and the blessings through Moses; ib. יוכיחן משה … והת' ביד ישראל let Moses who loves them rebuke them, and Balaam who hates them, bless them in order that the blessings and the rebukes be made certain in Israel’s hand; Yalk. ib. 795. Deut. R. l. c. הואיל וקבלו עליהן תּוֹכְחוֹתֶיךָ וכ' because they accepted thy (Moses’) rebukes, thou must bless them; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>
